climate_pressure: Climate-mitigation-driven coal transition, not a physical climate hazard.
documented_impact: The World Bank anticipates job losses and worker/family dislocation in coal-dependent regions if transition is poorly managed.
fcv_mediator: Dependence on coal, unequal adjustment opportunities and reduced access to social/economic services can distribute transition costs unevenly.
possible_consequence: The source warns of possible mistrust, insecurity and social instability without mitigation; it does not document realized conflict.
alternative_explanations: Wider economic change, labour conditions, service provision and governance can independently affect trust and insecurity.
uncertainty: Prospective 2023 executive-summary mechanism. No measured transition-related violence, causal effect or emissions scenario; this is distinct from physical-hazard risks. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: The report identifies inclusive local governance and knowledge as capacities; social/economic mitigation is a proposed safeguard, not an evaluated peace outcome.
compact_statement: In coal-dependent East Kalimantan and South Sumatra, a poorly managed mitigation transition could transmit job/service losses through unequal adjustment into mistrust and instability; the World Bank frames this as prospective risk, not observed conflict.
